Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows complete opacification ("white-out") of the left hemithorax with a contralateral tracheal shift to the right, which is the classic radiographic presentation of a massive pleural effusion pushing the mediastinum away. Atelectasis or lung collapse would typically cause an ipsilateral (leftward) tracheal shift due to volume loss, while pneumothorax would appear radiolucent rather than opaque.
